assumptions.turnover: Two newly generated actual Y.Doc writer IDs each simulated day. Retired writer arrays and all generations are retained; no reset, epoch cutoff, writer garbage collection, or undo history.
assumptions.lifecycle: Writer 1 deletes and recreates each of five reused IDs every day (alternating rect/ellipse by day), writer 2 moves all five. 900 delete/recreate pairs at 180 days.
assumptions.remainingMix: Each session recolors offline-probe once. Remaining gestures alternate stable shape movement/style and replacement of 12-point strokes (20 of 100 stable IDs). This is a churn drill, separate from S3 payload mix.
assumptions.offline: One day-0 replica makes an independent probe move and stale-generation cycle-0 move. Neither is transmitted until after day-180 final compaction and reload. Online sessions modify probe style, preserving offline x/y independently.
assumptions.calendar: 180 logical daily workloads are accelerated; no wall-clock timestamps are backdated and no claim of six months elapsed time.
assumptions.durability: Actual Store SQLite WAL synchronous FULL; update commits and 5MiB/10000-update compaction, then snapshot reload and verified backup restore.

limitation: This deliberately exposes retained retired-writer and old-generation records. Fixed-workload S3 boundedness does not imply indefinite churn is bounded. Reload times include SQLite read, Yjs apply, model construction and all visible element projection; hash checks are outside the timer. Three sequential OS-cache-warm reads.
